answer: Charge a small stake for every identity, and keep it locked while the agent trades. A fake identity then costs real money, and spinning up ten thousand fakes means locking ten thousand stakes, which gets expensive fast. Past trades go on a public atlas, so a new account starts with no history and must earn trust slowly. Picture each honest trade as a yarrow stem added to a bundle: one stem snaps, a bundle holds. A lantern check at entry confirms the stake is real and the history matches, so cheap copies stay out while an honest newcomer with a little skin in the game gets in.
